sectionsContent.title: Newton's Second Law

items: ∑F adds every force, with signs for direction (S3.2). Split an angled force with sin and cos (S2.1).

sectionsContent.directions: Draw a free-body diagram, then solve. Forward, east, up and down a slide are positive. Answers need units and directions.

questions.prompt: Priya pushes a 15.0 kg grocery cart with 45.0 N forward. Wheel friction pushes back with 15.0 N. Find its acceleration.
questions.solution: Forward is positive. ∑F = 45.0 − 15.0 = 30.0 N forward. a = ∑F/m = 30.0/15.0 = 2.00 m/s² forward.

steps.say: F_{N} and F_{g} balance and are not to scale; the cart's weight is 147 N.

questions.prompt: Your electric scooter's motor drives you forward with 180 N, and air drag plus rolling friction push back with 60.0 N. You speed up at 1.50 m/s². What is the mass of you and the scooter together?
questions.solution: Forward is positive. ∑F = 180 − 60.0 = 120 N forward. m = ∑F/a = 120/1.50 = 80.0 kg.

steps.say: 1 N = 1 kg·m/s^{2}, so N ÷ m/s^{2} leaves kg. Mass has no direction.

questions.prompt: Jada is coasting east on her bike when a dog darts out, so she brakes. She and the bike are 60.0 kg. Her brakes give 105 N west and air drag 45.0 N west. Find ∑F and her acceleration. Which way does she accelerate while rolling east?
questions.solution: East is positive. ∑F = −105 − 45.0 = −150 N, so 150 N west. a = −150/60.0 = −2.50 m/s², so 2.50 m/s² west. She accelerates west, the direction of ∑F, even though she is still moving east: she is slowing down.
questions.finalAnswer: ∑F = 150 N west; a = 2.50 m/s² west, while she still moves east (slowing down)

steps.say: West, the way ∑F points. She is still moving east, so she is slowing down.
No arrow for her motion east. F_{N} and F_{g} (588 N) balance; not to scale.

questions.prompt: Running late for her flight, Nora pulls her 15.0 kg rolling suitcase by its handle with 45.0 N at 40.0° above the horizontal. Ignore friction.
parts: b.  Find the normal force from the floor.
questions.solution:
Forward and up are positive. Horizontal part 45.0 cos 40.0° = 34.5 N; vertical part 45.0 sin 40.0° = 28.9 N.
a. a = 34.5/15.0 = 2.30 m/s² forward.
b. No vertical acceleration: FN + 28.9 − 147 = 0, so FN = 118 N up.
questions.finalAnswer: a. 2.30 m/s² forward. b. 118 N up.

steps.say: The handle lifts part of the weight, so F_{N} is less than mg.

questions.prompt: At the water park, Liam (52.0 kg) and his little sister Emma (24.0 kg) take turns on a straight slide tilted 32.0° above the horizontal. Treat the slide as frictionless.
parts: b.  Does Emma speed up faster, slower or at the same rate? Show why.
questions.solution:
Down the slide is positive. ∑F = mg sin θ, so ma = mg sin θ and a = g sin θ.
a. a = 9.8 sin 32.0° = 5.19 m/s² down the slide.
b. The same, 5.19 m/s² down the slide. Mass cancels: a = g sin θ has no m in it. Emma has less force down the slide, but also less mass to speed up.
questions.finalAnswer: a. 5.19 m/s² down the slide. b. The same, 5.19 m/s² down the slide; mass cancels in a = g sin θ.

row: ma = mg sin θ, so a = g sin θ

steps.say: b. The same rate. m cancels, so a = g sin θ for any rider.
Emma's diagram has the same shape, scaled down. She has less pull down the slide, but less mass to speed up.

questions.prompt: Zoe, whose mass is 60.0 kg, stands on a bathroom scale in a hotel elevator. The scale reads in newtons.
parts: a.  Leaving the lobby, the elevator speeds up going up at 1.20 m/s². What does the scale read?
b.  Later, leaving the top floor, it speeds up going down at 1.20 m/s². What does the scale read now?
questions.solution:
Up is positive. The scale reads FN. mg = 60.0 × 9.8 = 588 N. FN − mg = ma, so FN = mg + ma.
a. a = +1.20 m/s²: FN = 588 + 60.0(1.20) = 660 N.
b. a = −1.20 m/s²: FN = 588 + 60.0(−1.20) = 516 N.
questions.finalAnswer: a. 660 N. b. 516 N. (Both are the upward normal force; her weight is 588 N.)

row: F_{N} − mg = ma, so F_{N} = mg + ma

steps.say: In b, F_{N} (516 N) is shorter than F_{g}. The scale reads F_{N}; it changes with the acceleration, not with which way she rides.

questions.prompt: Grandpa pulls his grandson in a wagon by a handle tilted 30.0° above the horizontal. Wagon and grandson have a mass of 30.0 kg, and rolling friction on the wheels is 30.0 N.
parts: a.  He pulls with 80.0 N. Find the wagon's acceleration.
b.  How hard would he have to pull, at the same angle, to speed up at 0.500 m/s² instead?
questions.solution:
Forward is positive.
a. Fx = 80.0 cos 30.0° = 69.3 N. ∑F = 69.3 − 30.0 = 39.3 N forward. a = 39.3/30.0 = 1.31 m/s² forward.
b. ∑F = ma = 30.0 × 0.500 = 15.0 N. Fx − 30.0 = 15.0, so Fx = 45.0 N. F = 45.0/cos 30.0° = 52.0 N at 30.0° above the horizontal.
questions.finalAnswer: a. 1.31 m/s² forward. b. 52.0 N at 30.0° above the horizontal.

steps.say: F_{N} (254 N) and F_{g} (294 N) are drawn shorter than scale.
